item.title: Rome ramps up security around Colosseum with new ‘red zone’ targeting criminals
item.description: Rome's new red zone around the Colosseum targets predatory crime and disorder after a violent July 1 confrontation involving roughly 50 people.
item.content:encoded:
Rome has declared a "red zone" around the Colosseum after predatory crime, drug dealing and a violent confrontation involving roughly 50 people turned one of the world’s most famous tourist destinations into a security flashpoint.

The "enhanced-control zone" covers the Colosseum, Imperial Forums and Colle Oppio and allows authorities to remove certain people whose violent, threatening or persistently disruptive behavior creates a public safety risk, according to a six-page order issued by Rome Prefect Lamberto Giannini.

The measure took effect Aug. 24 and will remain in place for four months, through Christmas Eve.

FIREWORKS REPORTEDLY TRIGGER MASS HORSE STAMPEDE THROUGH ROME STREETS, INJURING SEVERAL SOLDIERS

Officials said the area has experienced a "resurgence of disorder" that was "predominantly attributable to groups of young people of non-EU origin," according to the order.

The document cited predatory crimes, fights and fireworks near the ancient amphitheater, warning that the explosives may have been used to distract potential crime victims.

Officials said the trouble reached a breaking point July 1, when Rome Capital police officers responded after fireworks were set off near the Colosseum. A group of approximately 50 non-EU nationals allegedly resisted responding officers and damaged police property, according to the order.

The group surrounded local police officers and left two with minor injuries during what news agency ANSA described as an unauthorized gathering in Piazza del Colosseo.

Authorities also singled out Largo Gaetana Agnesi, a terrace overlooking the Colosseum and situated above the Colosseo subway station, as a regular gathering place for the groups at the center of the security concerns.

The nearby Colle Oppio park was also described as a problem area because of people officials said may be engaged in conduct harmful to public safety and public order.

SEATTLE MAYOR ANNOUNCES CRACKDOWN ON CRIME-PLAGUED NEIGHBORHOOD AFTER YEARS OF COMPLAINTS

The newly designated zone stretches through some of the most recognizable areas of central Rome, including Piazza Venezia, Via dei Fori Imperiali, Piazza del Colosseo, the Arch of Constantine and Piazza del Campidoglio.

Giannini issued the order following a proposal from Rome’s police chief and discussions by the Provincial Committee for Public Order and Security.

The order says the opening of the Metro C station serving the Colosseum has also contributed to the security challenges by creating a direct connection between the historic center and neighborhoods in eastern Rome.

The station and another subway stop inside the designated area draw large numbers of commuters and tourists who could be exposed to criminal activity, officials said.

TOURIST HOT SPOT SLAPPED WITH US TRAVEL WARNING RENEWAL DUE TO CRIME AND TERROR

Under the order, authorities may remove people who engage in violent, threatening or persistently disruptive behavior and who were reported during the previous five years for specified offenses. Those include intentional crimes against people or property, certain drug offenses, weapons violations and crimes carrying a particular hate-crime aggravating circumstance.

The order is part of a broader push to protect residents and a flood of tourists visiting the Italian capital. Officials described Rome as facing an unusually complex security situation because of major international and historic events, the heightened geopolitical threat environment and the continuing influx of visitors.

AMERICAN TOURISTS STABBED OUTSIDE ATHENS' ACROPOLIS AS POLICE DETAIN SUSPECT IN APPARENT RANDOM ATTACK

Authorities said ordinary patrols, surveillance systems, fixed security posts and joint "High Impact" operations had produced results but had not stopped repeated criminal conduct or fully restored public spaces to residents and visitors.

Officials also extended a separate security zone in Esquilino, covering streets around Rome’s main Termini train station and the Basilica of Santa Maria Maggiore.

ITALY SHUTS DOWN EFFORT LINKED TO GAZA FLOTILLA GROUP TO TRACK JEWISH, ISRAELI TOURISTS

Officials said demonstrations around Termini continue to require close attention. They also cited the increased number of visitors and pilgrims traveling to Santa Maria Maggiore, where Pope Francis is buried, warning that large crowds can become targets for predatory crimes.

An earlier enhanced-control designation covering the Valle Aurelia area, including the Battistini and Cornelia subway stations, was discontinued after authorities determined that continuing the special measures there was no longer useful.

Anyone who violates the order could face criminal charges under Italian law.

Fox News Digital reached out to Rome police for additional information.

item.title: MLB tells umpire Doug Eddings he made a mistake in demanding Cardinals pitcher straighten his hat
item.description: Umpire Doug Eddings told rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon to fix his tilted hat during his MLB debut, sparking an ejection and a reportedly rebuke from the league.
item.content:encoded:
It's not often you see Major League Baseball criticize umpires or an individual umpire, as the league office prefers to downplay any mistakes or poor calls. But what veteran umpire Doug Eddings did on Friday during the Colorado Rockies-St. Louis Cardinals game apparently warranted such unusual treatment.

Eddings inserted himself into the game, apparently believing that fans buy tickets to see umpires, when Cardinals rookie reliever Hancel Rincon entered the game to make his major league debut. Rincon had his had tilted to the side, obviously not the traditional way to wear a baseball hat, but hardly anything exception or unusual in the modern game. Bizarrely, though, Eddings felt it necessary to instruct him to fix it.

Cardinals manager Oli Marmol was unsurprisingly furious, rushing out to defend the 24-year-old pitcher. Marmol could be seen telling Edings to "grow the f*** up" before getting tossed from the game, then went off about Eddings behavior afterward.

HOT MIC CATCHES HEATED ARGUMENT BETWEEN MLB MANAGER AND UMPIRE AFTER CONTROVERSIAL EJECTION

"I had an issue with Doug," he said to the media after the game. "Just Doug. He took it upon himself to tell our rookie pitcher the kid’s ‘not going to wear his hat on my field that way.’ You got Dontrelle Willis, CC Sabathia, Pedro Strop -- plenty of guys that have worn it way more tilted. I have an issue with that. That’s just a power-hungry move, in my opinion."

Eddings then defended himself by telling reporters that he'd made the decision to step in after a hitter from the Rockies complained about the hat.

"The batter said, ‘Hey, can he wear his hat like that?’" he explained after the game. "I really didn't know, but it was really, really crooked. I asked the catcher to tell him to straighten his hat out, and the pitcher did. Nobody said anything until he gave up a couple runs."

Except only one Colorado player had been up to the plate when the warning was issued, Hunter Goodman, who promptly denied he'd said anything.

"I never once mentioned the hat," Goodman told reporters. "It doesn’t matter who’s pitching. I don’t care how they wear the hat. I’m trying to find out where the ball is coming out, and I’m trying to worry about what I’m doing in the box. I’m not worried about how his hat looks.

"It was one of those situations — it’s kind of a wild, wild thing that happens in the game. But I didn’t like seeing that my name was a part of it today when I didn’t say anything like that. You watch baseball growing up. There are a lot of guys who have had their hat crooked or however. Honestly, before today, when I went back and looked, I didn’t even notice the hat was messed up or looked like that when I was hitting. Anyway, I don’t pay attention to that stuff."

From Rincon's perspective, he addressed it by saying that Eddings had "apologized" to him and that he'd put the incident behind him.

CINCINNATI REDS PITCHER RIPS 'F—ING FATA–' UMPIRE FOR GETTING IN DEFENDER'S WAY ON GROUND BALL

"I understood a couple words and it looked like he apologized to me for what happened last night, and he also told me good luck the rest of my career as a big leaguer," Rincon said. "I told him don't worry, it's nothing personal, and everything stays here."

Still, in a very obvious gesture, many Cardinals players wore their hats purposefully tilted in the dugout before Saturday's game, and seemingly added a celebratory helmet tilt when reaching base.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

On Sunday, the Athletic reported that MLB had formally spoken to Eddings and told the veteran umpire he'd gone too far by telling Rincon to fix his hat.

Ken Rosenthal spoke to sources within the league about the incident, writing, "Umpires operate with broad discretion if they believe a player's actions are distracting, but according to two people briefed on the matter who were granted anonymity because they are not authorized to speak publicly, the league viewed Eddings' admonishment of Rincon as going too far."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Frankly, it did go too far. Wearing a hat tilted a bit one way or another isn't an offense, and as Marmol brought up, it's hardly unprecedented. Is it every baseball fan's preferred way for a professional to wear a hat? No, of course not. But it isn't the type of infraction that warranted Edding's reaction.

Maybe Eddings thought he heard someone from the Rockies complain about the hat and took it upon himself to say something? Or maybe he thought it was some sort of violation then had to backtrack afterward?

Regardless, Rincon pitched again Saturday, with his hat tilted to his liking. Eddings, still part of the umpiring crew over the weekend, let it go.

item.title: Socialism 2026 speaker slams diet industry for policing 'Black fat flesh,' calls it 'body fascism'
item.description: A Socialism 2026 speaker argued that policing "Black fat flesh" anchors entire systems of governance, calling modern health standards body fascism.
item.content:encoded:
An activist at the Socialism 2026 conference in Chicago slammed the "diet industry" for policing "Black fat flesh," characterizing modern health standards and weight management as forms of "body fascism".

During a session on "Health Fascism" on Saturday, author Da’Shaun L. Harrison said that the policing of "Black fat flesh" is foundational to broader "entire systems of governance." 

"Black fatness is made meaningful through suffering, through surveillance, and through control and the policing of Black fat flesh anchors entire systems of governance. Without a population to discipline, there would be no BMI, no obesity epidemic, and no medical or scientific institutions organized around managing fatness," Harrison said.

"The diet industry reflects this logic. It operates through what I once defined as formal and informal relationships among major food corporations, the medical-industrial complex, and individual wealthy benefactors to sustain a social order in which fat people are monitored, restricted, guilted, stolen from, and punished. Diet culture has always linked food to morality, framing restraint as virtue and pleasure as danger through language like 'guilty pleasure,'" Harrison said.

DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ERUPT OVER 2028 ENDORSEMENT AS AOC SPECULATION GROWS: 'DANGEROUS PATH'

The four-day Socialism 2026 conference, held at the Hyatt Regency McCormick Place and organized by Haymarket Books, brought together activists, organizers, and communities from across the country and around the world, featuring over a hundred participatory discussions, lectures, and workshops, according to the event's website.

Harrison was one of three panelists — alongside podcast co-hosts Beatrice Adler-Bolton and Artie Vierkant—who spoke during a session titled "Health Fascism, Body Politics, and the Anti-State State". Over 200 people attended the discussion, which formed part of the conference's broader "Health Fascism" series. Clips of the conference were shared on X by Manhattan Institute investigative analyst Stu Smith.

"As governments retreat from care, and health increasingly becomes a signifier of discipline—rather than provision—fitness, disability, fatness, illness, Blackness, impairment, and bodily capacity are mobilized into measures of moral worth and political belonging. This panel examines how health, disability, body size, and race are instrumentalized by the state and being reorganized under health fascism," according to an event description.

In the session, Harrison argued that diet culture conditions "obedience," "self-denial," and "discipline" before framing those concepts as central components of "body fascism." 

JILLIAN MICHAELS EXPOSES DANGERS OF SELF-DOSING ILLEGAL 'GRAY MARKET' WEIGHT LOSS DRUGS

"Abstaining from pleasure becomes a way to train obedience, to train self-denial, and to train discipline in service of a broader political order. Body fascism is not some relic of the past. It's an active feature of modern imperial regimes," Harrison explained.

Harrison also criticized GLP-1 weight-loss drugs like Ozempic, contending that efforts to treat fatness as a public-health issue are intrinsically connected to racial control.

"Every time a government decides whose body must be protected and whose bodies must be erased for the sake of national imagery, this is body fascism. Every time there is a call for sovereignty by state powers with the intent to maintain borders, this is body fascism. Every time Black flesh is wrangled, dismembered, abused, this is body fascism. Understanding this clarifies exactly how fascist ideologies operate through the body, not only by glorifying a narrow ideal, but also by violently repressing the Black fat," Harrison added.

Jonathan Alpert, a psychotherapist and author of "Therapy Nation," told Fox News Digital that Harrison's comments are a byproduct of ideology infiltrating everything.

"There are fair criticisms of BMI and how it’s used. But calling it ‘body fascism’ is what happens when ideology gets inserted into almost every part of life," Alpert said.

"We’re seeing more and more ordinary issues viewed through the same lens: Who has power? Who’s oppressed? How does race factor into it? Now even a conversation with your doctor about weight or diet can be framed as a form of oppression," he added.

"That fits neatly into the worldview being promoted at a conference like this. Instead of seeing people primarily as individuals who make choices and have some responsibility for their lives, everything gets explained through systems, identity and power," Alpert said.

"Socialism may be an economic philosophy, but the culture surrounding this version of it goes much further. Personal problems become political problems, and individual responsibility gets pushed aside in favor of identifying the system or group supposedly responsible," he explained further.

"As a psychotherapist, I think there’s a psychological cost to that. If you teach people to interpret uncomfortable information as an attack, they become less willing to hear things they may need to hear. Sometimes a doctor telling you that you need to lose weight or change your diet isn’t racism, oppression or an attempt to control your body. It’s medical advice," Alpert added.

Harrison and representatives for the Socialism 2026 panel did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s requests for comment.

item.title: Trump appears to debut darker hair, sparking online buzz
item.description: New photos of President Trump stepping off Air Force One with what appeared to be a darker hairstyle have quickly fueled social media buzz.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump appeared to debut a darker hair color Friday, sparking widespread speculation online after stepping off Air Force One in New Jersey ahead of a weekend at his Bedminster golf club.

Known for his signature blond hairstyle, Trump was photographed arriving at Morristown Municipal Airport with what appeared to be a noticeably darker, more brunette look —prompting a flood of reactions across social media.

"Trump becoming a brunette was definitely not on my 2026 bingo card," one user wrote on X.

"This was Donald Trump yesterday while departing to New Jersey for the weekend! Look at the appearance of his hair! Is he getting a new hair color?" another user wrote.

HOUSE DEMS PLOT TRUMP INVESTIGATION BLITZ IF THEY SEIZE MAJORITY

"Seems brown is the new blonde ...," a third user added.

"Trump is now a brunette!" another post read.

Photos shared on Instagram by internet personality Michael Solakiewicz showed Trump golfing Saturday in a red hat that covered most of his hair, making it difficult to tell whether the darker look remained.

TRUMP’S PENTAGON SHAKE-UP REVIVES A PRESIDENTIAL POWER PLAY WITH A LONG HISTORY

The online speculation comes just days after Trump pushed back on allegations that he wears a wig, pointing to a windy 2024 campaign rally in Ohio, according to The Hill.

"I don’t wear a wig. But that night, they found out I did not wear a wig because if you did, it was not going to be on your head very long," Trump said Wednesday.

Trump has rarely made noticeable changes to his appearance while in office.

TRUMP NEGOTIATORS WITKOFF, KUSHNER MEET WITH PUTIN IN MOSCOW AS US PUSHES FOR END TO RUSSIA-UKRAINE WAR

In 2019, he sparked similar speculation after appearing with what looked like a slicked-back hairstyle during a surprise visit to a Virginia church.

That hairstyle was short-lived. Trump spoke to reporters later in the day wearing his usual hairdo.

The White House could not immediately be reached by Fox News Digital for comment.

Fox News Digital's Bradford Betz contributed to this report.

item.title: Kansas State Wildcats' mascot forced to complete absurd amount of push-ups during 71-3 victory
item.description: Willie the Wildcat cranked out 394 push-ups after Kansas State scored 71 points against Nichols State, and he could barely raise his arms by the end.
item.content:encoded:
If you were one of the lucky ones to see your college football team score more than 70 points this weekend - and judging by the offenses we saw on Saturday, that likely isn't many of you - then you're probably feeling pretty good right now.

Everyone loves watching the scoreboard light up and the ball get marched up and down the field (as long as it's your team doing the scoreboard lighting and ball marching).

One guy - or anthropomorphic cat - who isn't feeling too great about all that scoring is Willie the Wildcat.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S FIRST FULL SATURDAY IS HERE AND IT'S A CELEBRATION OF AMERICA AT ITS BEST

You see, he's the mascot for the Kansas State Wildcats, and his boys had themselves a night on offense.

71 points to be exact, all at the expense of poor little Nicholls State.

The Colonels got absolutely smoked, but the only person more upset than their defense about that offensive performance is probably dear old Willie.

That's because Willie had to do some work, busting out a set of push-ups to match the scoreboard after every scoring drive.

TENNESSEE TITANS REVAMPED THEIR MASCOT AND SOCIAL MEDIA CERTAINLY HAD SOME THOUGHTS

And by the end of the night, our calisthenically inclined mascot could barely go through his range of motion.

71 points is a lot on its own, but 394 push-ups (someone else did the math for me) in one night is downright mental unless you're prime Arnold Schwarzenegger.

Willie might be the only mascot in America that will be joining the players in the cold tub Sunday morning.

I know some people are clowning him for his form, but I'd like to see you keyboard warriors bang out 400 push-ups and still be able to even raise your arms above your head, let alone drop and give me seven more.

A LIST OF THE BEST COLLEGE GAMEDAY SIGNS AT LSU DURING SHOW'S 500TH EPISODE

If the Wildcats ever need a backup middle linebacker, Willie might be able to fill in admirably.

I'm sure Willie will be thrilled to see his team play a defense with a pulse, but K-State plays in the Big 12, so he might want to ice up and hit the protein shakes a little harder this season.

Good luck, buddy! We are rooting for you!

item.title: Group of fans kicked out of Portland Thorns NWSL match over pro-women apparel labeled 'transphobic'
item.description: Video shows eight fans in XX-XY Athletics gear ejected from a Portland Thorns FC match at Providence Park after LGBTQ organizer lobbied officials.
item.content:encoded:
A group of eight people was confronted at their seats and ejected from a Portland Thorns match at Providence Park after stadium security flagged their pro-women apparel.

Footage obtained by OutKick shows Amy E. Sousa attempting to speak with a venue staff member for about a minute as the group sat in their assigned seats for the NWSL match against the Washington Spirit.

Attendees were wearing gear from XX-XY Athletics alongside shirts bearing slogans such as "Save Women's Sports," "Girls just wanna have fundamental rights," "Woman," and "It's common sense."

WNBA ADMITS SECURITY IN ATLANTA WAS WRONG TO MAKE FANS COVER SHIRTS AT DREAM-FEVER GAME

In the video, venue staff hand the group a card notifying them of an infraction of the Providence Park and NWSL Code of Conduct before escorting them out of the building.

The notice gave venue staff 72 hours to contact the group about additional penalties. It also warned that refusing to provide personal information on the spot could lead to a ban from all future events at the stadium.

Sousa later told OutKick that she was accused of being transphobic.

ADF SENDS LETTER TO WNBA AFTER CONTROVERSIES OVER TREATMENT OF SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SUPPORTERS

Following the ejection, Sousa took to social media to push back against any claim that the group caused a disturbance inside the venue before security stepped in.

"We did nothing. We had not even shown our shirts. We were dressed like this when ejected," Sousa posted on X in response to the incident.

WNBA FANS RECALL EJECTION THREAT OVER XX-XY ATHLETICS SHIRT AT FEVER-DREAM GAME: 'I WAS FLABBERGASTED'

The episode at Providence Park, which is owned by the City of Portland but operated by a private company, raises questions about how speech rules are enforced at a publicly owned stadium.

Fans face a core question: Who polices game-day gear, and when does safety cross into overreach? The incident also highlights a contrast in how Portland’s sports teams handle fan attire.

Sousa previously attended a WNBA game at the Moda Center between the Portland Fire and Indiana Fever wearing her XX-XY Athletics shirt. She was even featured on the arena’s massive jumbotron during the live broadcast, while the Thorns later booted Sousa and the other fans from Providence Park for wearing similar pro-women apparel.

"I didn't take it seriously," Sousa said regarding online warnings she received before Sunday's match. "I was like, what are they going to do? Arrest us for watching soccer?"

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM SHARES TOUCHING MOMENT WITH YOUNG FEVER FAN AFTER GAME AGAINST PORTLAND

The security response at Providence Park followed public social media posts from a local LGBT group organizer, Hannah Perry, who lobbied municipal and state officials to intervene at the city-owned stadium.

Ahead of game time, Perry fired off a Facebook message to Sousa letting him know she’d already put the Portland PD, the mayor and Gov. Tina Kotek on notice.

Perry added that she was contacting Providence Park directly, alongside local organizations, to demand the group be removed. She called Sousa a "pathetic excuse of a human being" and wrote, "I hope that you're not allowed into the stadium."

Under the NWSL Fan Code of Conduct, spectators are prohibited from displaying signs, symbols, words or imagery used for political campaigning or advocacy. However, neither the league nor venue rules provide an objective standard for what turns basic slogan apparel into banned political expression, leaving enforcement largely to staff discretion.

Requests for comment sent to Providence Park venue management, Portland Thorns and NWSL league headquarters were not immediately returned.

item.title: Why Tasers sometimes fail to stop suspects — and what weight has to do with it
item.description: Multiple Taser deployments failed to stop Pamela Cisneros in the Times Square stabbing, raising urgent questions about how body composition can impact effectiveness.
item.content:encoded:
Multiple Taser deployments failed to stop Pamela Cisneros, 49, during a roughly four-minute standoff in Times Square last Monday, after she allegedly stabbed two people. The attack left a 32-year-old woman dead and a 68-year-old man wounded.

"As multiple officers discharged Tasers, which proved to be ineffective, the subject continued to advance toward our officers with the knives," Jessica Tisch, New York City police commissioner, said in a news conference that evening. 

When the Tasers failed to subdue Cisneros — who stated, "I’m not dropping anything. I would rather kill both of you" — two officers opened fire, striking her. Cisneros was taken to Bellevue Hospital, where she was pronounced dead.

NYPD IDENTIFIES WOMAN KILLED IN TIMES SQUARE STABBING SPREE

The incident sparked broader questions about why Tasers sometimes fail and whether obesity or body composition can impede their effectiveness.

A standard Taser is designed to fire two small, barbed probes connected to the device by insulated, conductive wires, according to Axon, the manufacturer.

"Electrical pulses travel along those wires and into the body, triggering involuntary muscle contractions," Axon’s website states. "For NMI to occur, it is best that two probes make contact 12 inches (30 cm) or more apart."

Steve Keller, a retired police sergeant in Blue Ash, Ohio, said the most common causes of Taser failure include clothing, probe placement, substance abuse by the perpetrator and connectivity between probes.

However, obesity can affect the Taser, he said, as a large layer of body fat could interfere with the connectivity.

"The purpose of the Taser is neuromuscular in capacity," Keller told Fox News Digital.

"Your large muscle masses are your back and thighs. Officers are trained to aim for those areas," he said, just as they are also trained to adjust their aiming for clothing and the distance between them and the subject.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

If one of the probes hits the abdomen and the person is obese, it can affect the connectivity of the two probes, according to Keller.

"If one probe hits the person and the other probe misses, the Taser will not work," he said.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

For example, if one probe hits a subject in the thigh and the other probe hits a thick bubble jacket, there’s a good chance the officer won’t have good connectivity, Keller said.

"The same could be considered if there is a large layer of body fat — they could still feel it, but it might not be as effective."

Referring to Cisneros’ case, Keller emphasized that mental health may also play a significant role in how a person responds to a Taser.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Tisch confirmed at the press conference that the suspect had a documented mental health history with the NYPD, with one incident in 2018 and another in 2019.

Dr. Marc Siegel, Fox News senior medical analyst, agreed that body composition can affect the Taser’s effectiveness.

"Tasers are much more effective for muscle than fat because muscle conducts electricity much better, and the Taser delivers a high voltage," he said. "In an obese person, it is more difficult to find an area that conducts electricity."

Fox News Digital reached out to Axon, the NYPD and obesity organizations requesting comment.

item.title: MLB legend Alex Rodriguez reveals the foods he keeps in his kitchen fridge
item.description: MLB legend Alex Rodriguez revealed his fridge staples, from eggs, water and fruit to hummus, plus a pantry loaded with chips he enjoys at 2 a.m.
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball (MLB) All-Star Alex Rodriguez, better known as A-Rod, hasn’t swung a bat professionally in a decade, and he revealed he eats a lot less than he did when he was a full-time athlete.

"During my 25-year career, I ate a lot more," the legendary MLB slugger, three-time MVP and World Series champion told Men’s Health in a video showing what he keeps in the refrigerator and pantry of his Los Angeles, Calif., home.

"I used to eat six times a day — a lot of steak, a lot of potatoes, a lot of rice, beans," A-Rod said. "You’re burning so much calories when you’re playing 162 games."

TENNIS GREAT RAPHAEL NADAL SWEARS BY BREAKFAST WITH NUTRIENT-PACKED TINY FISH

These days, the 51-year-old businessman, sports-team owner and broadcaster eats a wide variety of foods, with healthy options always on hand along with a stash of indulgent snack items.

The staples A-Rod told Men’s Health are always in his fridge include plenty of water — "some sparkling, but not too much" — eggs, spring lettuce mix and fruit, including bananas, apples and oranges, which the athlete called "very important."

He said he usually eats three or four meals a day and mixes in a protein shake.

His refrigerator still contains a few "pop sodas" (his term) for friends who visit, because A-Rod gave up drinking soft drinks five years ago.

Other items A-Rod said he must have in his fridge are blueberries — "always fresh, organic" — strawberries, greens — including salad and some broccoli — and hummus for a late-night snack.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

A-Rod said he is a "chips expert."

In his pantry, he unveiled an assortment of salty, greasy goodness in the form of barbecue chips, Doritos, Cheetos, Tostitos, Corn Nuts and cashews.

"This is where I do my best work — at 2 a.m.," he joked. He also acknowledged eating in bed.

One item A-Rod said you’ll never see in his kitchen is liver.

His standard breakfast includes eggs, some oatmeal, bacon, a little glass of orange juice and lots of water.

For lunch, he usually has some salad with balsamic vinaigrette dressing and chicken or fish.

For dinner, he likes steak or salmon with sweet potato fries — or "any type of fries, actually" — and said he doesn’t cook any of it, joking that he would probably start a fire.

A-Rod said he’s never tried a diet.

"I love to eat," he said. "I have a great relationship with food."

He added that while he was playing in the MLB, he used to "overeat" because he needed the energy.

"Today I probably under-eat," he said, "which is not good. I need to eat more, especially some healthy proteins, more fruit, more water, more fuel."

A-Rod said his favorite pregame meal was a peanut butter and jelly sandwich with barbecue chips and two bottles of water.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

To celebrate big wins, he said he enjoyed eating a big steak with a sweet potato "or some good sushi."

His go-to comfort foods reflect his Dominican heritage and include rice and beans, plátanos maduros — sweet, ripe plantains that are fried until caramelized — and tostones — twice-fried, crispy green plantains.

Revealing his go-to burger meal, A-Rod said it’s a double Whopper with cheese. He noted that he likes Burger King’s burgers but prefers McDonald’s French fries.

The sports star is a big coffee drinker, estimating he consumes between seven and eight cups a day. He also likes a Celsius energy drink before hitting the gym.

A-Rod said he incorporates protein shakes with protein powder, fruit and a little bit of peanut butter into his day.

He also takes vitamin C supplements, a multivitamin and, to help him sleep, some magnesium.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

His preferred ballpark food is a hot dog, specifically a Dodger Dog (served at Los Angeles Dodgers baseball games at Dodger Stadium).

"I also like a great pretzel," he said. "Nice and warm and big."

The "A-Rod special" is an unusual item you likely won’t find on a restaurant menu.

The baseball star’s "weird" favorite food combination is a peanut butter and jelly sandwich with deli turkey on it.

item.title: Amy Acton campaign says armed individual lunged at Ohio governor candidate, injuring multiple people
item.description: Amy Acton's campaign says the Ohio governor candidate was targeted by an armed individual at the Canfield Fair as political violence fears mount.
item.content:encoded:
An armed individual lunged at Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton and injured multiple people Sunday in a burst of violence at the Canfield Fair, her campaign said.

"While attending the Canfield Fair, an armed individual lunged at Dr. Acton, injuring multiple people," Acton campaign communications director Addie Bullock said in a statement.

"Dr. Acton and Eric are grateful for the swift and decisive action of law enforcement and are praying for the recovery of those injured," Bullock added. "This kind of violence has no place in Ohio. Dr. Acton will always stand up to the chaos, hate and vitriol that pits us against one another."

TRUMP'S DECADE OF ASSASSINATION THREATS RUNS FROM BUTLER SHOOTING TO LATEST GOLF CLUB BREACH

Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine later confirmed that Acton was not hurt and said he and first lady Fran DeWine spoke with her following the incident.

"Fran and I are thankful Dr. Amy Acton was not hurt, and we send our thoughts to those who were injured," DeWine said. "We spoke to Dr. Acton this afternoon and she said to share with Ohioans that she is ok."

DeWine said a man "tried to forcefully push himself toward Dr. Acton" as she was speaking and injured other attendees at the Mahoning County Democratic booth.

"We are grateful for the quick work of the Ohio State Highway Patrol and other law enforcement on the scene at the Canfield Fair today," the governor said.

"Violence or the threat of violence at political or public events is always unacceptable," DeWine added. "This case is now in the hands of law enforcement and will be investigated thoroughly."

Officials did not immediately identify the man or say whether he had been arrested. Acton’s campaign described him as armed, although DeWine did not mention a weapon. The conditions of those injured were also unclear.

It was also unclear what prompted the confrontation and whether anyone had been arrested.

The incident came as Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned that candidates and other public figures continue to face threats as campaign season kicks into high gear.

"You’re never safe in the public eye," Mullin told Fox News’ Peter Doocy during an interview on "The Sunday Briefing."

WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS’ DINNER SHOOTING LATEST IN YEARS OF ATTACKS TARGETING TRUMP, CONSERVATIVES

Doocy asked Mullin whether candidates were safe heading into the traditional Labor Day weekend kickoff to campaign season, citing the political assassinations and assassination attempts that have rocked the country in recent years.

"If you read any of the social media posts, which I choose not to, but you see the type of rhetoric and the hatefulness that’s out there," Mullin said.

DEM SENATE HOPEFULS UNDER SCRUTINY FOR ‘CHOKE THEM OUT’ RHETORIC AFTER TRUMP ATTACK SCARE

"The threats to our elected officials, they don’t go away," he continued. "We’ve got to bring down the temperature, but the temperature is not going to go down on itself."

Mullin said Americans must accept that political disagreements are part of the country’s system of government while drawing a firm line at violence.

WEST VIRGINIA MAN PLEADS GUILTY TO MAKING VIOLENT THREATS AGAINST TRUMP, ICE

"The American people have to realize that we do have a republic, and the republic has different opinions, and it’s OK to have different opinions," he said.

"When you cross a line and say that that different opinion needs to be silenced — it needs to be silenced through violence — that’s where Homeland comes into place," Mullin added. "Free speech is something we all protect, but there’s a line that you can cross that goes from free speech to inciting dangerous behavior."

Mullin was speaking broadly about political threats and was not responding directly to the reported confrontation involving Acton.

Republican gubernatorial nominee Vivek Ramaswamy and his running mate, Ohio Senate President Rob McColley, condemned the Canfield Fair incident.

"Candidates should be able to meet with voters without having to worry about threats or violence," Ramaswamy campaign communications director Connie Luck said in a statement.

"What happened today is completely unacceptable and has no place in politics, and we hope that no one was hurt," she added.

RAMASWAMY OUTLINES KEY CONTRASTS WITH DEM OPPONENT LESS THAN 100 DAYS OUT FROM KEY GUBERNATORIAL ELECTION

Acton and Ramaswamy are facing off in November’s closely watched race to replace term-limited Republican Gov. Mike DeWine.

Acton, a physician, became a household name in Ohio while serving as director of the Ohio Department of Health during the COVID-19 pandemic, according to The Associated Press. She appeared alongside DeWine during televised briefings as the state imposed shutdowns and other public-health restrictions.

Her handling of the pandemic has since become a central campaign issue, The AP reported. Ramaswamy and other Republicans have criticized Acton over the restrictions, while her campaign has defended her work with DeWine as necessary to protect Ohioans.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Mahoning County Sheriff’s Office for additional information.

Fox News' Peter Doocy contributed to this report.

item.title: Andrew Garfield faces backlash after telling billionaires to be 'scared' of his new movie
item.description: Video captures Andrew Garfield saying he hopes billionaires are "scared shitless" by his new film "The Uprising" about the Peasants' Revolt.
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Garfield took heat on X after calling out "billionaires" while discussing his new movie, "The Uprising," Thursday at a Los Angeles film screening.

In a video uploaded by film review website, The Movie Report, Garfield and director Paul Greengrass answered questions about the historical action drama that depicts England's 1381 Peasants' Revolt. The story takes place in the aftermath of the Black Death, when heavy taxes imposed by King Richard II's court to fund the Hundred Years' War push impoverished commoners to a breaking point.

"What's your dream takeaway for people in the audience when they go home?" an audience member asked Garfield, adding, "What are you hoping for?"

LEWIS HAMILTON, WORTH $500M AND DATING BILLIONAIRE KIM KARDASHIAN, WANTS TO PUT 'A LIMIT' ON WEALTH

"Well, first I hope they come and see it, first thing," Garfield responded. "Secondly, I hope it's galvanizing. I hope there's some awakening that people feel … that we all feel like our own struggles are being reflected in the struggles of these characters from a distant time and place and that it could be directive."

"And I hope that if any billionaires watch it, they're scared sh--less," Garfield added.

Garfield’s remarks sparked swift backlash, with critics highlighting the substantial wealth the movie star has accumulated throughout his career.

TRUMP SAYS HE HOPES SPENCER PRATT DOES WELL IN LA MAYORAL RACE, BLASTS CALIFORNIA'S 'RIGGED' ELECTIONS

"When I first heard they were making a period film about Wat Tyler, I was pretty excited. But the more Andrew Garfield talks, the more it sounds like it's just going to be socialist garbage," said Rick Davis, an associate pastor at Providence Church in Lynchburg, Virginia. (Garfield plays a fictional lead character named Ploughman in the film, while actor Cosmo Jarvis portrays historical rebel leader Wat Tyler).

Spencer Pratt, a former candidate for mayor in Los Angeles, pointed out what he viewed as irony in Garfield’s statement.

"You mean…like the billionaires who greenlight your movies and stroke all your multi-million dollar paychecks? Or they good?" Pratt wrote. He added, "Ironically, Garfield just got paid like $5M for playing billionaire Sam Altman in Artificial."

SPENCER PRATT DUBS HIMSELF THE 'FRESH PRINCE OF BEL-AIR' IN SPOOF CAMPAIGN VIDEO FOR LA MAYOR RACE

"Hilarious that world-famous, multi, multi millionaire Andrew Garfield is cosplaying as a put upon member of the working class," Substack columnist John William Sherrod posted.

"More billionaires were involved in making this than will probably ever watch it," Noam Blum, chief technology officer at Tablet Magazine also posted.

Garfield has starred in major blockbuster films including "Spider-Man: No Way Home," "Hacksaw Ridge," and "The Amazing Spider-Man."

Neither Garfield nor Greengrass responded to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: Team USA basketball survives scare against Italy in FIBA Women's World Cup, secures quarterfinal berth
item.description: Caitlin Clark finished with just one point as Team USA barely survived Italy's upset bid in a dramatic 55-52 FIBA Women's World Cup thriller.
item.content:encoded:
Team USA got all it could handle from Italy in Sunday's FIBA Women's World Cup game.

The Stars and Stripes jumped out to a 19-8 lead by the end of the first quarter and held on to win by a score of 55-52, though the contest wasn't without its fair share of lead changes and controversies.

Italy led by three midway through the fourth quarter and even had a chance to tie the game on the final shot where an Italian player looked like she may have been fouled.

CAITLIN CLARK NOT IN TEAM USA'S STARTING 5 FOR FIBA WOMEN'S BASKETBALL WORLD CUP OPENER VS CHINA

But the game-tying attempt sailed to the left of the rim and landed harmlessly into the arms of Breanna Stewart, ending the threat.

Team USA shot a putrid 1-12 from beyond the arc (8%) and only made 29% of their field goals overall, highlighting just how much work still needs to be done if this team wants to make a run at the title.

ANGEL REESE VS. 7'3" DOUGHY CHINESE TOWER ZHANG ZIYU WAS A BATTLE FOR THE AGES AT THE FIBA WORLD CUP

Italy's Cecilia Zandalasini led all scorers with 14 points to go along with seven rebounds and was the unquestioned star in a game full of them.

For the Americans, Jackie Young led with a team-high 10 points and was the only player to shoot above 40% from the field.

CAITLIN CLARK AND ANGEL REESE MUST NOW WORK TOGETHER AT WOMEN'S WORLD CUP AS WNBA TAKES A HIGH-STAKES BREAK

Had the Italians hung on to win, it would have been one of the most monumental upsets in FIBA Women's World Cup history.

With the win, the U.S. women improved to 2-0 in group play and have now qualified for the quarterfinals of the tournament.

Time will tell if this group of women has what it takes to bring some hardware home from Germany, but if they don't want to leave empty-handed, they will need their heavy hitters to step up, namely Caitlin Clark, who finished with just one point and was held without a field goal for the entire game.

item.title: Has National Championship picture in college football already changed after a stunning first week?
item.description: Lane Kiffin's LSU obliterated Clemson as the National Championship race was reshaped by shocking week one results from Michigan, Oregon and USC.
item.content:encoded:
Week one of the 2026 college football season isn't fully in the books, and already the playoff and National Championship picture has already been turned upside down. And the balance of power within the two top conferences might have shifted, unexpectedly, after some shocking performances, both good and bad.

While the Indiana Hoosiers are defending national champions, finished off a 16-0 season, and brought in another impressive transfer portal class under Curt Cignetti, most have expected that the Big Ten Championship will run through two other programs: the Ohio State Buckeyes and Oregon Ducks.

Ohio State lived up to the billing, with an overwhelmingly dominant win over Ball State. Far from a top opponent, sure, but the Buckeyes did exactly what they needed to as the country's number one team in their opening game. Oregon though? Not exactly.

OREGON RALLIES FROM SLOW START, THWARTS BOISE STATE'S UPSET BID IN SEASON OPENER

The Ducks struggled for most of the first half against Boise State, then found themselves tied with just over eight minutes to go in the game after a Broncos field goal. But after a quick touchdown drive to take a 34-27 lead, the Oregon defense stiffened, and closed out the win with back-to-back stops. That said, the Ducks dominated more than the scoreline indicated. They averaged nearly eight yards per play, allowing just 4.2 to Boise State. They had 10 yards per attempt passing, with 28 completions on 38 attempts for 378 yards, while adding three sacks and four tackles for loss on defense. The scoreline was close, but Ducks fans can be encouraged that they "deserved" a more decisive outcome.

Then there's the "second tier" of the Big Ten, teams that have hoped coaching staff changes and another year of development for start quarterbacks will make the difference: Michigan and USC. SC brought in defensive coordinator Gary Patterson to finally make the Trojans defensive unit championship quality. Michigan, after a year of turmoil after the firing of Sherrone Moore, hired Kyle Whittingham away from Utah, a head coach known for his consistency and steadiness.

Their outcomes on Saturday couldn't have been more different.

Nobody who watched Michigan, outside fans of the program, thinks they escaped Western Michigan with a last-second win. They were outplayed, couldn't get the Broncos offense off the field, frequently benefited from questionable officiating, then required a miraculous Hail Mary, that should never have happened, to escape with the win. Even including that 47-yard pass, the Wolverines had just 276 yards of offense. At home. Against Western Michigan as a 28-point favorite.

CLOCK CONTROVERSY ALLOWS MICHIGAN WOLVERINES TO AVOID MASSIVE UPSET AGAINST WESTERN MICHIGAN

They averaged 5.8 yards per play, again, with that 47-yard pass included. Bryce Underwood, making an enormous amount of money after a high-profile recruiting war, looked awful. Excluding the Hail Mary, Underwood had 11 completions on 21 pass attempts for 123 yards. Against Western Michigan, at home. The Michigan running game, long a point of pride in Ann Arbor, had 16 attempts from its running backs, for 59 yards. At home. Against Western Michigan. Broncos running back Jalen Buckley had 19 carries for 62 yards. By himself.

A sloppy early season performance isn't enough to fully end a team's season, just ask Notre Dame in 2024, who lost 16-14 to Northern Illinois, then played in the College Football Playoff National Championship game. But with most observers treating Michigan's performance as a loss, and a tough schedule with Oklahoma next weekend, games against Iowa, Penn State, Indiana, Oregon, and Ohio State, it's hard to see the Wolverines as a realistic contender for a playoff spot.

USC though? Their defense finally put in the type of performance fans have been waiting for.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Fresno State isn't Oregon, of course, but the Bulldogs were expected to be one of the better Group of Six teams. They finished 2025 at 9-4, beat Boise State 30-7 and Oregon State 36-27. Many believed they could compete near the top of the newly reconfigured Pac-12 Conference, with analyst Greg McIlroy picking them as the G6 playoff representative.

But the Trojans ran them off the field. SC were 21-point favorites, then outgained the Bulldogs 552-116. They averaged 8.1 yards per play, while allowing just 2.6. Most of Fresno's offensive stats came from the last drive of the game against the SC backups. Midway through the fourth quarter, the Trojans defense had allowed just over 50 total yards on offense and 1.7 yards per play. Fresno State isn't an FCS team. They were No. 73 in preseason SP+, one of the best analytics-driven ranking systems available. That's ahead of teams like Stanford and USF, and not far off from Colorado and Iowa State.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

USC has a tough road ahead too, with games against Oregon, Washington, Ohio State, Indiana, and Penn State ahead, but if the Trojans defense is for real, they might suddenly be, finally, "back."

LSU HAD A REVIVAL, CLEMSON WAS AT A FUNERAL: LANE KIFFIN’S DEBUT SENDS A LOUD MESSAGE TO COLLEGE FOOTBALL

No question though, the most impressive of the weekend had to be the LSU Tigers. Despite the controversy surrounding the program, Lane Kiffin's debut couldn't have been better. LSU obliterated Clemson, who were hopeless offensively, and barely able to provide opposition defensively. The Tigers treated the other Tigers like an FCS team, and immediately cemented themselves as top contenders in the SEC, along with Texas and Georgia.

Nothing's decided in week one, but we did, already, see the playoff picture get a shakeup. LSU and USC might be better than expected, with both providing more competition for Ohio State and Georgia than many believed heading into the season.

Oregon, while they clearly "deserved" the win, seem a bit further away from championship quality than many projected based on the talent Dan Lanning's accumulated. And Michigan, well, if poll voters were honest about what everyone saw, they deserve to fall out of the top-25 entirely.

item.title: Hasan Piker brushes off Dems who see him as a liability, names his '28 choice
item.description: Hasan Piker told Fox News his job isn't to help the Democratic Party, even as consultant James Carville called him "an idiot" who isn't a Democrat.
item.content:encoded:
Hasan Piker hears the growing chorus of Democrats condemning him for incendiary statements, and he has a message for the party: "My job is not to make the Democratic Party look good."

The far-left Twitch streamer has boosted socialist candidates even as he created headaches for the broader Democratic Party in a midterm election cycle where it hopes to make major gains. The 35-year-old Piker — whose polarizing stances range from defending communist Chinese dictator Mao Zedong to comparing Zionism to "Nazism" — is a darling of the Democratic Socialists of America, but a potential liability for mainstream Democrats as November approaches.

Piker said Democratic Party officials have not reached out to coordinate a strategy.

"I have not had a conversation with anyone from the DNC," Piker said. "That would be very funny."

JAMES CARVILLE DECRIES 'IDIOT' HASAN PIKER, ORDERS DSA TO CHANGE ITS NAME

In an exclusive interview at the 2026 Socialism Conference in Chicago, Piker told Fox News that, while he tries "to be as careful as possible" when it comes to choosing his words, his hours-long streams present his opponents with the "perfect opportunity to create viral media moments."

Some of those moments include intense backlash over Piker’s 2019 statement that America "deserved 9/11," a comment which has been widely condemned by politicians on both sides of the aisle.

HASAN PIKER CALLS REPUBLICAN PARTY THE 'BIGGEST DOMESTIC TERRORIST' IN THE COUNTRY

Piker acknowledged that he should not have used the word "deserved," but said his point was that "[America’s] meddling in the affairs in the Middle East actually transpired these horrifying events."

"It's not a controversial thing [to argue]," Piker said. "It was the language that I used that was controversial."

HASAN PIKER CALLS HAMAS 'FAR MORE MODERATE,' DISMISSES TERROR GROUP’S BRUTAL RULE IN GAZA

Piker's brash commentary gives him credence with the far-left DSA, which pulled off a host of primary victories against more moderate Democrats, but party elders have disavowed him.

"There’s two things that I know about Hasan Piker," longtime Democratic Party consultant James Carville told Fox News Channel last week. "One, he’s an idiot, and two, he’s not a Democrat. So, I don’t answer for idiots, and I don’t answer for people who are not Democrats."

VAN JONES WARNS FAR-LEFT SOCIALIST AGENDA IS 'REGRESSIVE' THREAT TO DEMOCRATIC PARTY

Key Democrat lawmakers, including House Minority Leader Hakeen Jeffries, senators Cory Booker, D-N.J., and Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., and several House members have condemned Piker's past rhetoric.

As he crosses the country, joining campaign rallies and canvass launches for liberal challengers to establishment-backed candidates, Piker acknowledged that even his allies have urged him to moderate his rhetoric for the sake of their electoral chances.

DEMOCRATS' CIVIL WAR HEADS TO MICHIGAN WHERE PROGRESSIVES FACE BIGGEST TEST YET IN HIGH-STAKES SENATE SHOWDOWN

But Piker told Fox News the press is overstating his association with the progressive political candidates and wondered why the media had not "demanded condemnations from establishment Republicans for collaborating with Charlie Kirk or using him as a campaign surrogate."

Piker campaigned hard for Abdul El-Sayed, the progressive Michigan Democratic Senate nominee who pulled off a major upset victory against the establishment-backed Rep. Haley Stevens, D- Mich., in August. While his active support for El-Sayed may have generated buzz among Piker's base, it's also led El-Sayed to face a barrage of questions and criticism about his association with Piker.

GRETCHEN WHITMER ENDORSES MODERATE HALEY STEVENS IN TIGHT UPCOMING SENATE PRIMARY

Piker said that while he is confident El-Sayed – who distanced himself from Piker in recent weeks – will win this fall, "if people want to blame me" in the event El-Sayed loses, "they can blame me," adding, "I think that's the goal."

Piker's role in the midterms may prove to be a warmup for the 2028 presidential election, and he said he has no plans to moderate his stances or stay on the sidelines. He said he will back socialist Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y. if she launches a bid for the Democratic Party's presidential nomination.

WATCH: AOC WON'T RULE OUT WHITE HOUSE BID AFTER POLL NAMES HER DEMOCRATS' TOP 2028 PICK

"I think she's great," Piker said. "She would have some difficulties, of course, but hurdles can be climbed over, and I think she can do it."

Piker believes his influence will continue to grow, and predicted even Democrats now condemning him will "try to utilize the platform that I have" if they seek higher office in 2028.

2028 BATTLEGROUND POLL SCRAMBLES DEMOCRATS’ FUTURE AS INSURGENT SOCIALIST SEIZES LEAD

"And I'm not talking about my ideological allies or people who are associated with me right now," he added.

item.title: Stray bullet from nearby lounge fight kills Frito-Lay worker inside Sam's Club
item.description: Nashville police say a Frito-Lay worker was killed by a stray bullet inside Sam's Club after an argument spilled outside Lavo Lounge on Antioch Pike.
item.content:encoded:
A deadly argument outside a Nashville lounge sent a bullet tearing through the metal wall of a nearby Sam’s Club, killing an innocent Frito-Lay worker as he counted products in the chip aisle, police said.

The victim, identified as 55-year-old Paris Carlock of Murfreesboro, was conducting an early-morning product inventory near the middle of the store shortly after 4 a.m. when the bullet struck him in the head.

Sam’s Club staff rushed to Carlock’s aid before he was transported to a local hospital, where he was pronounced dead, according to the Metropolitan Nashville Police Department.

POLICE SEARCH FOR GUNMAN AFTER WALMART EMPLOYEE SHOT DURING DISPUTE IN PENNSYLVANIA

Investigators believe the gunfire was connected to an argument that began inside Lavo Lounge on Antioch Pike, just down the street from the Sam’s Club.

Police said security removed the people involved from the lounge, but the dispute reportedly spilled outside and continued. Gunshots were heard as multiple vehicles left the area.

MISSOURI MOM OF 5 FATALLY SHOT WHILE BUYING SLUSHIES WITH CHILDREN; POLICE SEARCH FOR GUNMAN

One of those bullets pierced the Sam’s Club’s exterior wall and struck Carlock as he worked inside, police said.

The department described Carlock as an "innocent" victim.

POLICE SWARM MICHIGAN SHOPPING CENTER AFTER 'SIGNIFICANT' SHOOTING INCIDENT; AT LEAST 2 DEAD

Homicide Unit detectives are pursuing leads, but police have not announced any arrests or released descriptions of the people or vehicles involved.

"We are deeply saddened by the passing of one of our colleagues," a PepsiCo spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "Our sincere condolences are with their family members and loved ones. We have been working closely with law enforcement and local officials regarding the matter."

Anyone with information about the gunfire or the vehicles seen leaving the area is asked to call Nashville Crime Stoppers at 615-742-7463.
